clue.text: One attending a meeting

parts.note: a 'meeting' here is a race meeting, a day of horse races, not a business gathering, and the clue describes someone who goes to it

explanation.surface: Someone sitting in on an office meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meeting' suggests a committee or conference; in racing a meeting is a day's card of races at one course.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who goes to the races is a spectator at a race meeting.

clue.text: Repair to Blackpool?

definitions.meaning: to repair to a place is to go there, to have recourse to it
Blackpool is a seaside holiday town in north-west England, given as an example, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: An invitation to head off to the seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repair' looks like fixing something; here it means to go, as in 'repair to the bar'. BLACKPOOL is a popular English seaside holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: To have recourse to something is to fall back on it; a holiday town by the sea is a seaside destination of that name.

clue.text: Bird caught by storm circling wild moor

indicators.note: circling says the pair of pieces before it go round the shuffled moor

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to storm is to rage or rant

indicators.note: wild signals that the letters of moor are scrambled

explanation.surface: A bird snatched up by a gale swirling over open moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' reads as weather in a moorland scene; it is the verb, to rage. 'circling' makes the caught-plus-storm pair wrap the shuffled moor, which sits just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A large dark fish-eating seabird is one species of water bird.

clue.text: Grand sedan in show

parts.note: G is a standard abbreviation for grand (a thousand)
a sedan chair is a litter, a seat carried on poles

explanation.surface: A grand saloon car on display at a motor show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sedan' suggests a car; here it is the old sedan chair, a carried litter.
explanation.definitionFit: Showiness or superficial sparkle is called glitter, as in the glitter of celebrity.

clue.text: One subtracted from one or the other to give this number

indicators.note: subtracted from tells you to take the first piece away from the phrase after it

parts.note: either means one or the other of two
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An arithmetic puzzle: take one from a choice to reach a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a figure, but it is a 'numb-er', something that numbs: ether was an early anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaesthetic deadens feeling, so it is a numbing agent, a 'numb-er'.

clue.text: … to agree to enter office

definitions.meaning: to consent or assent to a request
to take up a post, especially a throne, as a monarch does on succession

explanation.surface: Continuing a previous clue: someone persuaded to agree to take up a post.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots tie the surface to the previous clue; they play no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Consenting to a request and succeeding to a throne or post are both senses of the same verb.

clue.text: Revel's beginning to cause a stir

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of the word cause

parts.note: to stir feelings is to arouse them

explanation.surface: A party-goer's opening move is to make a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revel's' reads as a possessive; the 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel is to drink and make merry noisily, which is what a drinking spree involves.

clue.text: Faithful? Divorcee's given decree

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse, a divorcee
an act is a decree or statute

explanation.surface: A question of loyalty answered by a divorce court ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faithful' suggests marital fidelity in this divorce scene; it means accurate, as in a faithful copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A faithful reproduction is a precise, accurate one.

clue.text: Rod needs changes to be sanctioned

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of rod needs are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rod must alter his ways before he gets approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a person's name; it is just anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Approved or officially backed is the sense, as a candidate is backed by a party.

clue.text: Bad fracture? It could put one out!

parts.note: food gone bad has gone off
a fracture is a break

explanation.surface: A nasty broken bone that could knock someone out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an off-break is a ball that spins in from the off side and can get a batsman out; 'put one out' sounds like injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning cricket delivery can dismiss a batsman, putting him out.

clue.text: Frank's in front on the home stretch

indicators.note: on joins the second piece to follow the first in this across answer

parts.note: the home straight is the last stretch of a racecourse before the finish
forward means in front

explanation.surface: A runner called Frank is leading as the race enters its final stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank's' looks like a horse's name; it is the definition, with 's for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank means being open, direct and honest, without evasion.

clue.text: Bird (duck) in list

indicators.note: in tells you to place the duck inside the list

parts.note: a roster is a list of names and duties
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A duck has found its way onto a list of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'duck' looks like a second bird; it is O, a cricket score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is a male farmyard bird.

clue.text: Ranting? Could be subtler

indicators.note: could be says the letters of subtler may form another word

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a loud tirade might have been more delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud aggressive talk with little behind it is empty bluster, much like ranting.

clue.text: Union contract? Break one in anger

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or break

indicators.note: in says the one goes inside the pieces around it

parts.note: rage is anger
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A trade union deal, broken by a furious member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union contract' suggests trade unions; it means the contract of wedlock. 'in' puts the one just after the double R.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedlock is the union of two people under a binding contract.

clue.text: Stake with bound animal

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake
to lope is to run with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: A tethered beast tied to a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' and 'bound' suggest a tethered animal; they mean a poker bet and a loping stride.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift horned grazing beast of Africa and Asia is a kind of mammal.

clue.text: Best of people, literally

indicators.note: of signals the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A remark about the finest of humanity, taken word for word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best of people' looks like the definition; 'of' instead signals the letters run across 'people, literally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of a group, its top people, are the cream or best.

clue.text: Fashion model with line that's unpromising

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters of model and line are reshaped

explanation.surface: A catwalk model with a new clothing line that looks doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion model' reads as one phrase; 'Fashion' is the anagram signal and 'line' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boding badly, with bad omens, is inauspicious.

clue.text: Cuts up girl student, getting plastered

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word cuts is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a co-ed is a female student at a mixed college

explanation.surface: A violent scene: a student attacked, ending up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CUTS into STUC. 'Plastered' suggests drunk; it means coated in plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Walls covered with a fine render or plaster finish are coated in stucco.

clue.text: Carry first of medals, symbol evoking respect

parts.note: to tote is to carry

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of medals

explanation.surface: Wearing your medals as a token that commands respect.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved emblem of a clan or spirit is a revered object.

clue.text: Supervisor, a German, in new organisation

indicators.note: new organisation says the letters of a German are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A German supervisor appointed in a freshly formed company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word: the anagram of A GERMAN gives the supervisor.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss who runs a department or business oversees staff.

clue.text: Establish film sequence on part of ship

parts.note: a take is a single filmed sequence
the hold is the cargo space in a ship

explanation.surface: A film crew shooting a scene below decks.
explanation.definitionFit: To become firmly rooted or established, as an idea does, is to take root.

clue.text: Accommodation? A sprinkling round University

indicators.note: round says the sprinkling goes around the university letter

parts.note: hosing is a sprinkling with water from a hose

explanation.surface: Student accommodation getting a watering round the campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Places for people to live, collectively, are dwellings provided for them.

clue.text: Birds of prey, it's said, beginning to swoop

indicators.note: it's said marks a word that sounds like the one entered

parts.note: a hunting bird stalks its quarry as the opening move before it swoops

explanation.surface: Raptors circling, ready to begin a dive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birds of prey' reads as raptors, but only 'Birds' defines; 'of prey' sets the hunting scene for STALKS, which in British speech sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-legged wading birds with long bills are a family of large birds.

clue.text: Bit of a nut, they say, this officer

indicators.note: they say means a word that sounds like the piece is wanted

parts.note: a kernel is the edible inner part of a nut

explanation.surface: Gossip that this officer is a bit nutty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of a nut' reads as slightly mad; it is the inside of a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: An army rank above lieutenant colonel and below brigadier is a senior officer.

clue.text: Guided, say, over ridge

parts.note: led is the past of lead, meaning guided

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, flips the abbreviation for say

parts.note: eg (for example) is a way of saying 'say'

explanation.surface: Being led across a mountain ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow shelf jutting from a rock face is a ridge or projection.

clue.text: Epicure's cut fleshy fruit (paid for)

indicators.note: cut says the last letter of the fruit is lopped off

parts.note: a gourd is a large fleshy fruit
to meet a bill is to pay it, so met means paid for

explanation.surface: A food lover's sliced squash, already paid for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the D from GOURD to leave GOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur of fine food and drink is a gastronome.

clue.text: Greek possessed by a person's lost soul

indicators.note: possessed by sets the Greek letter at the front of the person who holds it

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for Greek
a oner is British slang for a single remarkable person

explanation.surface: A Greek man said to be possessed, a lost soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possessed' suggests demonic possession; it only places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond help or doomed is a hopeless case.

clue.text: An elder goes in PO — could be this one

definitions.text: An elder goes in PO — could be this one

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the phrase before it may form another phrase

explanation.surface: An elderly person walks into the post office to collect a weekly payment.
explanation.walkthrough: PO is the Post Office, where British pensioners traditionally collected their state pension; the whole clue both defines and shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired person drawing the state pension is an elderly recipient of that payment.

clue.text: Dull day, back end of July

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of July

explanation.surface: A grey day at the end of July.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull is gloomy, cheerless and boring.

clue.text: Ship reportedly helps to deliver army units

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds like the piece is wanted

parts.note: aids means helps

explanation.surface: A ship brings relief supplies to troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Military formations of several battalions are large army units.
